body.statement:
Assume \(p_0\in\operatorname{relint}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}})\), \(\operatorname{im}(B)\subseteq\operatorname{lin}(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{ASC}}-p_0)\), the local-family affine-hull condition, multinomial interiority, base convergence, compact-uniform centered local expansion, effective moving-offset encoding, and \(c_n\to0\).  Let \(R_n^{\diamond}\) and \(M_n^{\diamond}\) be defined by \(\mathrm{def:comparison\mbox{-}window\mbox{-}schedule}\) and \(\mathrm{def:windowed\mbox{-}multinomial\mbox{-}minimax}\).  These are diagonally selected expanding lawful windows, not asserted to be computable from the compact convergence hypotheses.  Then \(R_n^{\diamond}\to\infty\), every finite atomic Gaussian dual certificate has a lawful multinomial realization inside \(B_{R_n^{\diamond}}\), and
\[
 \lim_{n\to\infty}M_n^{\diamond}
 =M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0),
 \qquad
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n
 \geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
\]
If the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\mathrm{oeq:effective\mbox{-}compatible\mbox{-}density}\), or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package, is available, the Gaussian-rule and repair ingredients at any already selected window are replayable from \(\operatorname{CertGluePFL}\) receipts; no algorithm for selecting \(R_n^{\diamond}\) is claimed.  No conclusion about \(\limsup_nM_n\) follows from the stated compact-uniform premises.
body.justification: The corrected theorem states the strongest valid result: global liminf and two-sided convergence on certified expanding windows.
body.gap: An explicit hard seam escaping to infinity disproves the omitted global upper implication.
body.consumer: It determines the exact sampled-data interpretation permitted for the Gaussian minimax certificate.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: diagonal compact exhaustion, finite-support dual transfer, and exact windowwise repair.}
Write \(B_k=\{u:\|u\|_2\leq k\}\).  Fix \(k\).  The compact causal-domain lemma gives
\[
 B_k\subseteq\mathcal U_n
 \tag{23}
\]
eventually.  The positive-cell proposition gives, eventually,
\[
 \min_{u\in B_k}\min_{j\in\mathcal J}p_{n,j}(u)\geq\kappa/2.
 \tag{24}
\]
For each fixed \(\ell\leq k\), local expansion, zero-offset centering, and the compact remainder-and-covariance lemma make every term in \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\) tend to zero.  There are only finitely many \(\ell\leq k\); hence (23), (24), and \(\mathscr E_n(\ell)\leq1/\ell\) hold simultaneously for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The maximum defining \(R_n^\diamond\) is then at least \(k\).  Since \(k\) was arbitrary,
\[
 R_n^\diamond\longrightarrow\infty.
 \tag{25}
\]
This is a diagonal existence argument.  It does not compute the first index at which (23), (24), or the compact suprema pass their tests.  At the selected radius, however, the defining inequalities imply that the aggregate comparison error, denoted \(\rho_n\), satisfies \(\rho_n\to0\).

Let \(L<M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\).  Atomic duality supplies a finite Gaussian dual certificate \(\mu\) of value greater than \(L\).  Its finitely many coverage and risk support points lie in some \(B_k\).  Zero-offset centering and finite-arrangement stability realize each coverage atom carrying label \(v\) by a point of \(D_{n,v}\cap B_{k+1}\) at Mahalanobis distance tending to zero.  An equality atom is realized separately for every constraint role; the completed-face convention preserves all incident labels.

For a risk atom \(h\in H_{r_0}\), a lawful realization may also be chosen in \(H_{n,r_0}\).  If \(r_0>0\), the zero-offset semantic cells are cones and distance to each rival cone is positively homogeneous.  Replace \(h\) by \((1+t_n)h\), with \(t_n\downarrow0\) but large enough that the added distance margin dominates twice the directed-Hausdorff error.  Finite-arrangement stability then gives a nearby multinomial point whose distance from every rival union is at least \(r_0\).  If \(r_0=0\), uniqueness of the label at \(h\) and closedness of the finite rival union give
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_{\Sigma_0^{-1}}
 \left(h,\bigcup_{v'\neq v}D_{v'}^0\right)>0,
 \tag{26}
\]
so the same conclusion holds once the arrangement error is smaller than half (26).  By (25), all finitely many realized atoms lie inside \(B_{R_n^\diamond}\) eventually.

Apply Carter's reverse parameter-independent kernel to an arbitrary window-honest multinomial rule and then apply the score and covariance maps.  The bounded semantic-transfer lemma changes the finite dual objective by at most \(A_\mu\rho_n\), where \(A_\mu<\infty\) is the sum of the finitely many absolute dual coefficients.  Weak duality therefore gives
\[
 M_n^\diamond\geq L-A_\mu\rho_n.
 \tag{27}
\]
First let \(n\to\infty\), then let \(L\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)\), to obtain
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}M_n^\diamond
 \geq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{28}
\]

For the reverse inequality, fix \(a>0\).  Attainment gives a measurable \(K^a\in\mathcal C_{\eta_0}\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{h\in H_{r_0}}E_h\ell_0\{K^a(W_0)\}
 \leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a.
 \tag{29}
\]
The forward Carter kernel, Gaussian total-variation comparison, and finite-arrangement matching apply to every measurable randomized rule; no finite representation of \(K^a\) is needed.  By the defining tests for the selected window, its transfer has window coverage at least \(1-\eta_0-\rho_n\) and window separated risk at most
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n.
 \tag{30}
\]
At a separated-set boundary with \(r_0>0\), radial dilation restores distance \(r_0\), and the displacement is bounded by \(2R_n^\diamond\gamma/r_0\) when the distance deficit is \(\gamma<r_0/2\); this is one of the finite-arrangement terms tested before the radius is admitted.  When \(r_0=0\), (26) applies pointwise and incident chamber approximation plus Gaussian-shift continuity handles equality faces.  Thus (30) does not replace \(r_0\) by \(r_0-o(1)\).

Apply exact full-set mixing on the window with
\[
 q_n=\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
 \tag{31}
\]
The denominator is positive because \(\eta_0>0\), and
\[
 (1-q_n)(1-\eta_0-\rho_n)+q_n=1-\eta_0.
 \tag{32}
\]
Since \(0\leq\ell_0\leq1\), (30)--(32) yield
\[
 M_n^\diamond\leq M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0)+a+\rho_n
 +\frac{\rho_n}{\eta_0+\rho_n}.
 \tag{33}
\]
Letting \(n\to\infty\), then \(a\downarrow0\), and combining (28) and (33), proves
\[
 M_n^\diamond\longrightarrow M_{\mathfrak G_0,\eta_0}(r_0).
 \tag{34}
\]

Every globally honest rule is window-honest, and its global risk supremum dominates its window risk supremum.  Therefore the two minimax definitions give
\[
 M_n\geq M_n^\diamond.
 \tag{35}
\]
Equations (34)--(35) prove the asserted global lower limit.

Conditionally on the affirmative ECD conclusion, or on a separately proved sufficient package, CertGlue supplies a replayable finite Gaussian rule and exact repair for any already specified window; its transfer follows the same equations above.  This does not make the diagonal choice of \(R_n^\diamond\) computable, because the standing hypotheses provide no algorithms for the compact suprema or lawful-ball inclusion.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:escaping\mbox{-}boundary\mbox{-}kill}\) exhibits arrays identical on every fixed compact but with different global upper behavior.  It therefore rules out any global \(\limsup\) conclusion from the premises used here.
